Style presets are entire bundles of styl: Style presets are entire bundles of styles that you can apply to many elements. Normally, you set styles directly on elements, via the Design tab in the right sidebar. You can instead store some or all those styles in a style preset, and then apply the style preset to elements.
You can right-click styles or style sect: You can right-click styles or style sections to extract them into a style preset.
Style presets are a powerful way to let: Style presets are a powerful way to let you design faster and maintain consistency.
Variants let you design a page or compon: Variants let you design a page or component to look different in different conditions. For instance, a page can have a mobile variant or a French variant. A Button component can have hover/pressed states, or primary/secondary styles.
Use the on-canvas variant toolbar to tog: Use the on-canvas variant toolbar to toggle recording to any variant. Any edits you make while recording will override the component's "Base" (default) appearance. These overrides are indicated by a red colored dot.
Screen variants are a special variant gr: Screen variants are a special variant group that are based on screen size ("breakpoints") such as desktop vs. mobile.
If you want to re-theme the entire app,: If you want to re-theme the entire app, such as adding a dark mode, or a French language translation, you probably want to change many pages/components together.
Global variants are similar to normal (c: Global variants are similar to normal (component/page-specific) variants, except that global variants are global to the entire project: any component can have edits defined under a single “Dark mode” variant.
This lists all the combinations of varia: This lists all the combinations of variants that this component has recorded edits for. For instance, you might want a Button to have specific style settings when both the "Primary" variant and "Hover" interaction variant are activated.
You can specify arbitrary key-value pair: You can specify arbitrary key-value pairs as metadata for this page or component. Note: these are not page "meta tags"--these are arbitrary data for your code to consume from the headless API or in codegen (for any purpose). Learn more in the API docs.
Props enable you to customize individual: Props enable you to customize individual instances of a component. Reference props anywhere inside the component with dynamic values.
Use / in a prop name to organize props i: Use / in a prop name to organize props into folders, e.g. Header / title.
Element variants let you edit the styles: Element variants let you edit the styles of individual elements in special interactive states, such as hovered, focused, pressed.
(Component interaction variants are simi: (Component interaction variants are similar, but let you edit anything in the component based on the hover/focused/pressed state of the component's root element.)
You can import other Plasmic projects as: You can import other Plasmic projects as a dependency. The imported components are labeled as imported components, in the Components tab. Imported components are read-only. In order to edit these components, please visit their home project.
Attributes are non-style settings you ca: Attributes are non-style settings you can set on an element. Examples include hover text, ARIA attributes, and tab order.
Different types of elements have differe: Different types of elements have different attributes. For instance, with text inputs you can set placeholder text, with links you can set the URL, with buttons you can set whether it's disabled, and so on.
Slots let you fill in different instance: Slots let you fill in different instances of a component with different content.
Converting an element in a component to: Converting an element in a component to a slot target means you want to let component instances override that element.
This is where you can apply style preset: This is where you can apply style presets to the selected element.
This is where you can apply Custom Behav: This is where you can apply Custom Behaviors to the selected element. Use cases are general and varied. Examples: attach click-tracking to an element, or trigger a complex interaction, or apply an animated effect transform.
Underlying these are code components tha: Underlying these are code components that are meant to wrap around an element.
This section shows props for the parent: This section shows props for the parent Repeater component. You can use it to customize the elements which are being repeated.
This section shows URL parameters define: This section shows URL parameters defined in page path using brackets (e.g. [param]). In production, such parameters are defined based in the URL, but in studio you can customize what preview value they should have. For example, if your page path is /products/[slug] you can see how the page looks like and customize its styles using different "slug" values.
Add a path parameter like /item/ [id] to: Add a path parameter like /item/ [id] to accept URLs like abc.com/item/ 235.
Add a URL query parameter to accept URLs: Add a URL query parameter to accept URLs like abc.com/item/235? coupon=summer10.
Here you can also set the current previe: Here you can also set the current preview values for these parameters.
Add data queries to get data from a data: Add data queries to get data from a data source such as an API or CMS.
Legacy data queries ($queries) are depre: Legacy data queries ($queries) are deprecated. Please use the new data queries ($q) in the section above.
Use the Migrate all button, or Migrate i: Use the Migrate all button, or Migrate in an individual query's menu, to convert to new data queries with Plasmic AI.
Add data queries to get data from an int: Add data queries to get data from an integration like a backend database or API.
Create state variables to store any data: Create state variables to store any data that can change in your UI over time or as the user interacts. Update these from interactions, and connect your UI to them with dynamic values.
For instance, add a counter number varia: For instance, add a counter number variable that increments every time the user clicks a button. Set an element's text dynamic value to display the current counter.
This is where you can select what varian: This is where you can select what variant(s) to show on the selected component instance.
You can choose to use either the Loader: You can choose to use either the Loader or Codegen paths. The Loader path is only available for Next.js and Gatsby-based builds, and can greatly simplify deployments for most use cases. For all other React stacks, for users who want advanced customizability, and to be able to check Plasmic-generated code into your repository, choose the Codegen path.
(Loader is not available for existing re: (Loader is not available for existing repositories)
When you push a Plasmic project to a Git: When you push a Plasmic project to a GitHub repository, you can choose whether to make a pull request with the updated code generated by Plasmic or directly commit that code. This option sets the default behavior, but it can be overridden per push.
Images are any PNGs, JPGs, or non-colora: Images are any PNGs, JPGs, or non-colorable SVGs that you can use throughout your designs as pictures or background images.
Icons are colorable (but monochrome) SVG: Icons are colorable (but monochrome) SVGs that you can use throughout your designs.
User directories are lists of users and: User directories are lists of users and user groups. These are reused across projects in your organization or workspace.
